header:
Date: 2026-05-11
Start: 10:00 PDT
Duration: 72 minutes
Location: Virtual - All-hands
Attendees: Company-wide town hall (approx 150), leadership on stage: Maya Patel (CEO), Liam Chen (CTO), Sara Gomez (Head Product), Evan Ross (VP Eng), Priya Nair (Head People)
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto-transcript
summary: Short read: Leadership updated strategy adjustments for next quarter to prioritize reliability and cost control while maintaining dev experience. Announced a trimmed roadmap, hiring slow-down in non-critical roles, and a new customer pilot program for Redwood Private. Noted two recent incidents and immediate operational changes. Q&A covered SOC 2 auditor timing, Dedicated capacity SLAs, and whether we'll open a new EMEA region.
topics: Product roadmap trim and focus areas (Serving runtime, Optimize)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Monday — I know it's the usual time, we'll keep it tight, about an hour, we have a few big announcements and then Q&A. So I'm gonna start with the high level.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Quick frame: last quarter we grew fast, product adoption exceeded our model for hosted, traffic spiked in April and that exposed a few weak spots in our infra and our rollout cadence. We learned, and now we need to prioritize reliability and unit economics. Not glamorous but critical.
[00:40] Liam Chen: Yeah, to add — we saw two incidents that were different in root cause. One was scheduler cascading where KV cash— sorry KV cache thrash caused latency spikes; the other was a networking flake in a partner region. Both impacted customer p50/p99 in different ways. We're treating them as P1 learnings.
[01:04] Sara Gomez: From product perspective we're trimming the roadmap. We'll push some low-usage integrations and experimental UI features to next cycle, and double-down on batching, cache pre-warming, and the Optimize toolkit improvements that give immediate unit-cost wins.
[01:30] Evan Ross: Engineering actions: immediate guardrails on rollouts, canary percentage reduced, automatic fallback policy tightened, and a new runbook for cross-region failover. We'll also add a continuous latency regression job to CI for critical models.
[01:54] Audience - Speaker 1: Question — does this mean slower feature delivery for customers that asked for custom features? 
[02:03] Maya Patel: Good, yes, short term yes. We want to trade off some new surface area to keep SLOs strong. We'll still accept high-value enterprise requests via backlog prioritization.
[02:20] Priya Nair: People update — hiring will be focused. We are pausing non-essential headcount for the next six weeks, prioritizing roles that unblock reliability and sales-assisted enterprise deals. We'll re-open after the trimming period with updated bands.
[02:40] Audience - Speaker 2: Any comp changes? 
[02:45] Priya Nair: No changes to comp today; we will publish updated hiring bands and revised interview rubrics by the end of next week.
[03:00] Liam Chen: On the infra side, quick tech bullet points: kernel selection improvements landed for smaller sequence lengths, GPU memory gating to reduce OOMs during multi-tenant bursts, and a new quantization compatibility test harness. We'll also publish a perf sheet with new p50/p95 numbers by next Wednesday.
[03:28] Sara Gomez: Also launching a customer pilot for Redwood Private with three early enterprise partners — focused on VPC onboarding flow, KMS integration sanity checks, and audit-log harvesting. This is intentionally small so we can iterate.
[03:48] Audience - Speaker 3: SOC 2 status? timeline? 
[03:52] Evan Ross: We're targeting SOC 2 Type II by Q4, currently in readiness with a third-party auditor, gap remediation list is about 18 items heavy on logging and IAM gating. We'll share a compliance cut-down doc with security teams.
[04:12] Maya Patel: To be clear, enterprise contracts won't be blocked, but we'll augment attestations where customers need them.
[04:25] Audience - Speaker 4: EMEA region plan? 
[04:30] Liam Chen: We're evaluating two cloud partners for a focused EMEA roll. The timeline is contingent on cost and partner SLAs; expect a decision in six to eight weeks.
[04:46] Maya Patel: Financials quick note — we are tracking unit economics tightly. There will be fewer discretionary spend taps. We plan to reallocate budget toward infra and enterprise GTM where yields are highest.
[05:02] Audience - Speaker 5: Are we still investing in open source model contributions? 
[05:07] Sara Gomez: Yes but we'll do smaller, higher-leverage contributions (benchmarks, adapters) instead of large model releases.
[05:22] Maya Patel: Ok, switching to the incidents in a bit more detail — Evan?
[05:27] Evan Ross: The first incident was KV cache eviction storms — a combination of bad load shaping and an edge case in the cache eviction policy. We introduced immediate mitigations: conservative heap settings, better eviction prioritization. We're shipping a canary to prod by end of day.
[05:52] Evan Ross: The second incident was partner network flaps in a new region; we tightened routing rules and added graceful fallback to regional model variants.
[06:08] Audience - Speaker 1: Any customer impact refunds or credits? 
[06:12] Maya Patel: We'll handle on a case by case, CSMs are already engaged. No blanket credits yet.
[06:20] Liam Chen: Technically, we also found a monitoring blind spot: certain long-tail requests didn't hit our tracing hooks; we're adding trace sampling adjustments.
[06:34] Audience - Speaker 6: Question about Dedicated vs Hosted — are we scaling back Dedicated commits? 
[06:40] Sara Gomez: No, Dedicated is a priority for customers who need predictability; we will be more careful with capacity planning and offer migration assistance to variants during rollouts.
[06:55] Maya Patel: Onbed for leadership — we're increasing executive engagement on high-value accounts to accelerate renewals and ensure we get timely feedback from Dedicated customers.
[07:08] Audience - Speaker 7: Any immediate changes to pricing? 
[07:12] Maya Patel: No immediate pricing changes; we'll optimize behind the scenes (batching, quant). If there's a pricing revision it will be communicated well in advance.
[07:28] Liam Chen: Quick ask to the engineering org: please review the new canary checklist, it's now required for any model rollback/rollout that touches Dedicated infra.
[07:44] Priya Nair: People ops — we're adding more internal mobility slots to help redeploy folks from paused projects into infra, reliability, and GTM support roles. Managers will receive guidance today.
[08:00] Audience - Speaker 8: Remote-first policy - anything changing? 
[08:05] Priya Nair: Remote-first remains; we will run more local meetups in major hubs for knowledge transfer.
[08:15] Audience chatter / applause (indistinct)
[08:22] Maya Patel: Ok—let's open to questions from the chat; please be succinct.
[08:30] Audience - Speaker 9: How will we measure success for this refocus in 90 days? 
[08:35] Sara Gomez: Good question — primary metrics: p99 latency delta, cost per 1k tokens, time-to-recover for incidents, and # of enterprise rollouts completed. We'll publish the dashboard slice for company viewing.
[08:56] Audience - Speaker 10: Customer security audits — if a customer asks for an on-prem test, can we support? 
[09:02] Evan Ross: We can but plan is limited. For high-value deals we'll offer Private/on-prem pilots, but these are gated and require security sign-off.
[09:16] Audience - Speaker 11: Any new org hires to announce? 
[09:20] Maya Patel: We're welcoming a new Director of Solutions — name incoming later this week — and two senior SREs who've started.
[09:30] Audience - Speaker 12: Will we resume the hack days for infra? 
[09:34] Liam Chen: Yes, but they'll be targeted (observability, batching) not open-ended.
[09:42] Maya Patel: I'll close with a note — we're in a phase where operational excellence matters more than feature velocity. It's a bit uncomfortable but necessary, and it's the right call for product trust. Thanks for the candor.
[10:00] Maya Patel: Recap and next steps: leadership publishes hiring plan, product shares trimmed roadmap, ops runs incident tabletop. See the posted links in the slack #all-hands-summary channel. Thanks everyone.
notes: Shared artifacts: roadmap deck (link in slack), perf benchmark sheet (link to internal spreadsheet), incident postmortem draft (link), SOC 2 readiness checklist (link).
